title: hybrid-rag-kv-scrapbook
body:
Quick personal notes / messy scratchpad for hybrid RAG + KV-cache ideas. Intended to capture reading takeaways, initial experiment plans, and heuristics to test. NOT polished — mostly for my own reference and for talking points with Liam/Jinsoo before next sync.

Motivation:
- Many prod apps are hitting a tradeoff: large context retrieval (RAG) improves factuality but increases latency and costs when the model still has to attend to many retrieved chunks.
- KV caches (prefix or episodic caches) speed up autoregressive decoding for repeated contexts but are brittle when retrieval changes or when retrieved content diverges from cache keys.
- Can we design a hybrid flow: retrieval for coverage + dynamic KV stitching for short-term coherency, with graceful fallback when mismatches occur?

Key papers / posts skimmed (quick one-line takeaways):
- arXiv:2403.01234 — "Composable KV stitching" — shows improved token throughput when KV segments are reused across similar queries; but evaluation focused on synthetic dialog, not RAG.
- Blog: "Retrieval first, then cache" — practical tips for cache invalidation windows; recommends TTL ~ 10-30 minutes for session-based caching.
- SIGIR talk (2027) — "Hybrid retrieval+cache for low-latency QA" — canonical experiment: use retriever top-20, then select 3 anchors for KV encoding yields 2x latency improvement vs naive decode.

Rough architecture sketches (ideas):
1) Retriever -> chunk ranking -> dedupe -> 2-tier encoding
   - Tier A: hot anchors (3 best chunks) -> encode into KV segments and attach as prefix KV to model
   - Tier B: long tail chunks -> concatenate into condensed context for retrieval input or as separate retrieval query for reranking
2) Adaptive prefix length: if model historically attends heavily to first 512 tokens, allocate KV budget there; otherwise bias toward recent dialog turns.
3) Mismatch detector: cheap classifier (logistic / small FFN) that checks overlap between retrieved chunks and cached anchors; if mismatch > threshold, bypass KV stitching and do full prompt to avoid hallucination.

Hypotheses to test:
- H1: Using 3-5 anchored KV segments reduces tokens generated (per-request) by ~12-20% for multi-turn QA tasks with high repetition.
- H2: Mismatch detector reduces hallucinations vs always-stitching by > 30% while only increasing latency by < 10%.
- H3: Dynamic TTL (based on user activity) outperforms fixed TTLs for retention-efficiency tradeoff.

Experiment plan (minimal reproducible):
- Dataset: subset of Natural Questions + internal multi-turn support logs (anonymized). Create 2 splits: high-reuse dialogs vs low-reuse.
- Baselines: no-cache RAG (top-8 chunks), naive KV-stitch (always stitch top-3 encoded k/v), hybrid with mismatch-detector + TTL heuristics.
- Metrics: end-user latency (p95), tokens per response (model input + output), exact-match / F1 for fact answers, hallucination probes (manual eval), cost-per-1000-requests simulated.
- Implementation notes: reuse infer/runtime bench harness (see linked GH issue). Prototype with 8-bit quant model to keep infra cost low.

Small notes on mismatch detector design:
- Inputs: vector similarity between cached anchor embeddings and incoming top-k retrieved embeddings; token-overlap score between anchor text and retrieved chunk; last-turn user-probe features (length, type).
- Model: small MLP (2 layers, 128 hidden) trained on synthetic mismatch labels: label = 1 if gold answer depends on chunk not in anchors. Create labels from ablation on dataset.

Evangelism / product framing points (for short decks):
- "Smart stitch — get caching speed without stale facts"
- Lower unit-cost by reducing repeated decoding work while preserving retrieval coverage.
- Feature toggles for customers: prefer-latency vs prefer-quality; TTL sliders; mismatch-sensitivity knob.

Open questions / risks:
- How to handle retrieval-based updates (documents change) while caches persist? Need efficient invalidation hooks from doc-store (webhooks?)
- Edge-case: when retrieved docs contain contradictions — stitching may amplify hallucination if model over-weights KV anchors. Detector has to be conservative.
- Operational: collecting training labels for mismatch detector might require human-in-the-loop initially; how to bootstrap cheaply?

Next actions (Naomi -> short list):
- [ ] Build minimal prototype that: retrieves top-8, stitches top-3 as KV prefix, includes simple cosine-overlap mismatch rule. Target: 2-day spike. (owner: Naomi)
- [ ] Script evaluation harness for p95 latency + token-cost comparisons using existing bench infra. (owner: Jinsoo)
- [ ] Quick user-facing mockups of toggles and docs for Console. (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Sync with infra team on requirements for KV attach API (how to surface variable-length KV to runtime). Ping: @infra-kv.

Quick snippets / heuristics to try in spike:
- cos_sim(anchor_emb, retrieved_emb) < 0.7 -> treat as mismatch
- If user-session-active && hits-in-last-10min > 3 -> extend TTL to 20min else default 5min
- Budget: max KV tokens = 4096 across anchors (split proportionally by chunk-score)

Notes from last sync with Liam (2028-06-21):
- Liam: prefer deterministic eviction policy (LRU-ish per session) and test worst-case memory when many concurrent sessions attach anchors.
- Jinsoo: wants metrics instrumentation for anchor reuse rate & anchor-miss-to-hallucination mapping.

Scratchpad TODO for doc/email to PM:
- One-pager proposing RAG-hybrid spike with expected dev cost (2 engineers, 1 week) and success criteria (p95 latency reduction >= 15% on high-reuse cohort without >5% drop in factuality).

Random thoughts (for later):
- Could we compress anchors with learned dense summarizer then encode into KV? Might reduce KV budget but lose fine-grained facts.
- Explore learned gating inside model (adapter) to weight KV vs retrieved text at attention time — heavier engineering cost but elegant.

End of scratchpad. Will clean up if we decide to escalate to a JIRA/PRD.
